page.layout: One page of text: a Latin verse poem in italic, set full width above a rule; below the rule a heading "XVIII. GAL." and a French verse poem, in roman with a large initial. Right margin shows only faint show-through from the other side, which is left out. Printed page number at head left, running head at head centre, catchword at right below the last line.

p.i: Cui tot multiplici tument / Monstro colla truci? Quae fera vertices / Tot ceruice ferox gerit: / Cui centum radiat luminibus caput / Quodque: & cui variant sonos / Linguae dissimiles: semper & aurium / Cui diversa patet cohors? / Cur vestit viridi pectora pallio? / Cur nubes pice nigrior / Hydrae terga sequens tristia contegit? / Cur tam stulta volubili / Festinat geminos nixa pedes globo: / Velox quem subiti rotat / Cursu prae rapido temporis impetus? / Cui mors tela ferociter / Intentata manu lethifera iacit? / O, Mundi licet impares / Formas, & fluidam hic cernere imaginem.

main_text.head: XVIII. GAL.
main_text.p: CELVY qui pense pouvoir / Au Monde repos avoir, / Et assied son esperance / Dessus un tel changement: / Que pense un tel homme? il pense / Estre assis bien seurement

page.notes: The large initial of the French poem is C, joined to CELVY. The Latin poem is set in italic and runs as one piece with no stanza break. The catchword "Dessus" stands at the right below the last line and is not repeated in the text. Faint show-through from the reverse side at the right margin is not transcribed. The printed spellings "pouuoir", "auoir", "vn" and "ceruice" are normalised to u/v and i/j rules only as required; "pouvoir", "avoir" and "un" follow the u/v rule.
